extra: bytes beginning at pointer targets; their structure and full extent remain open

comments.text: Preserve X and Y, bank out I/O and copy twelve pages from RAM $D000–$DBFF to $1000–$1BFF, then four pages from $DC00–$DFFF to $0400–$07FF. Bank the KERNAL and I/O back in, restore Y and X and jump to $1000.
Copy Y plus one pages, starting at the source and destination encoded in the operands at $02DC–$02DD and $02DF–$02E0. Increment the high operand bytes after each page; X wraps through all 256 bytes.
Five 64-byte VIC sprite slots, pointers $3A through $3E in bank 1. Each slot supplies 63 bitmap bytes and a final unused byte; the captured airshaft frame reads these shapes.
The 63 bitmap bytes of sprite pointer $A2 in VIC bank 1: a narrow vertical line used in the captured airshaft frame. Each of the first 20 rows has one set pixel, followed by a blank row.
Sixty-three sprite bitmap bytes at VIC bank 1 pointer $AC, read by the captured airshaft frame; object unidentified.
Sixty-three sprite bitmap bytes at VIC bank 1 pointer $B4, read by the captured airshaft frame; object unidentified.
Character bitmap rows for glyph indices $00 to $22 in the airshaft character set. Each glyph is eight bytes; the captured frame reads this part of the set from VIC bank 1.

Bitmap rows for glyph indices $23 to $7F of the character set at $7000. Each glyph is eight bytes. In the captured frame the VIC uses bank 1 and selects this character set; these bytes match between the entry and play snapshots.

Bitmap rows for glyph indices $80 to $FF of the character set at $7000. Each glyph is eight bytes. In the captured frame the VIC uses bank 1 and selects this character set; these bytes match between the entry and play snapshots.

Initialise the airshaft scene: clear state and patched operands, set starting values, copy screen resources, configure VIC colours and bank, and start the interrupt before entering the main loop at $83E5.
Wait for the value at $8026 to change, advance the two-step counter at $803C, then select the next update path from that counter and state flags.

Copy the three patterns selected by the load operands at $8BE3, $8BE9 and $8BEF into the top eight rows of the sprite at $4180, then inspect $8031. Zero leaves the operands unchanged; one follows the increment path, and any other value follows the decrement path. Both paths clear $8031.
Advance the ones pattern by eight bytes, carrying to the tens pattern after digit 9. When both are 9, select digit 1 for the leftmost position and digit 0 for both lower positions, then clear $8031.

When the leftmost pattern is digit 1, restore the percent sign and set both lower positions to digit 9. Otherwise retreat the ones pattern by eight bytes, borrowing from the tens pattern when the ones pattern is digit 0; then clear $8031.
Save A, X and Y; inspect the stacked status and dispatch BRK through $0316 or IRQ through $0314.

Set VIC memory and display controls, sprite colours, positions and pointers, with two arrangements selected by $804A; call two helpers, acknowledge the raster interrupt and install $8E4A as the next IRQ handler at raster line $2B.

Set horizontal expansion and multicolour for sprites, position sprite 6, and optionally reposition sprites 1 and 3 when $804A is nonzero. Acknowledge the interrupt and set $8EB1 as the handler for raster line $3F.

Optionally restore sprite 5 and 6 colours, flip multicolour mode for sprites 0 to 3 and clear sprite 4 horizontal expansion; set positions, colours and pointers for sprites 0 and 4. Schedule $8F1F at the line calculated from $8F48 minus $29 and acknowledge the interrupt.

Set colours, positions and shape pointers for sprites 1 and 2, then acknowledge the interrupt and install $8F5E for the raster line held in the immediate operand at $8F48. The coordinate and pointer operands are patched during initialization.

Set sprites 0 and 1 from coordinates at $8027 and $8028, with sprite 1 offset by $18 horizontally; patch positions used by later handlers. Set their colours and shape pointers, adjust expansion and multicolour bits, then schedule $8FE4 and acknowledge the interrupt.
Eight-byte bitmap for digit 0, followed by digit 1; the mode drawing paths use these as source patterns.
Eight-byte bitmap for digit 2, followed by digits 3 and 4. The drawing code advances or retreats the source pointer in eight-byte steps.
Eight-byte bitmap for digit 5, followed by digits 6, 7 and 8.
Eight-byte bitmap for digit 9, the last of the ten decimal digits beginning at $928F.
Eight-byte bitmap of a percent sign. The upper status counter uses this pattern in its leftmost position when it is below 100.

Select a drawing path from the mode byte at $9166: mode 2 jumps to $956C, mode 3 to $95BA, and the remaining path updates once every four calls. That path copies eight source bytes into both columns at $41A8 and $41A9, spaced three bytes apart; its source addresses can be changed by later code.

Copy eight bytes from each of two source patterns into alternating columns at $41A8 and $41A9, three bytes per row. In the captured state the sources are $928F and $92B7. Additional state can alter the right-hand source address for a later call.
Clear $94BC, subtract eight from the right-hand pattern pointer in the load at $9570, clear the request at $94BE and return. The $958A path avoids the subtraction when that pointer is already $928F.

Copy eight bytes from each of two source patterns into alternating columns at $41A8 and $41A9, three bytes per row. In the captured state the sources are $928F and $929F. Additional state can alter the right-hand source address for a later call.
Clear $94BD, subtract eight from the right-hand pattern pointer in the load at $95BE, clear the request at $94BF and return. The $95D8 path avoids the subtraction when that pointer is already $928F.

If $960C equals 2, copy 21 bytes from $0F00 to $4240, increment $8018, add eight to the upper counter's tens-pattern pointer at $8BE9, reset $9612, set $9613 and call $9769. Otherwise continue at $9948.
Copy 55 bytes from $0F89 to $41C9, set the operands at $869C and $869F to $0FC9 and $41C9, clear $8045 and $9612, set $9613 and call $9769.
Copy 21 bytes from $0F15 to $4255, increment $8018, add eight to the upper counter's tens-pattern pointer at $8BE9, reset $9612, set $9613 and call $9891.
If $9611 is 1, add eight to the pattern pointer at $9571, clear $94BC and $9612, set $9613 and call $9891. Otherwise continue at $99F4.
If $9611 is 2, set both pattern pointers at $94E2 and $94E8 to $92D7, clear $94BB, $94C0 and $9612, set $9613 and call $9891. Otherwise continue to the 21-byte copy at $9A1F.
Copy 21 bytes from $0F2A to $426A, increment $8018, add eight to the upper counter's tens-pattern pointer at $8BE9, reset $9612, set $9613 and call $9891.
Add $14 to each 16-bit value at $A0CC and $A0CE. Decrement $8032; when it reaches zero, request a counter decrement by writing 2 to $8031 and reset $8032 to 2.
Subtract $14 from each 16-bit value at $A0CC and $A0CE. Decrement $8033; when it reaches zero, request a counter increment by writing 1 to $8031 and reset $8033 to 2.

Scan Q and P, then read joystick and Space into $8021 and $8022. A new Space press advances a three-position selection; joystick fire and directions choose the subsequent control paths. P waits for release, another press, and release again.
Advance $A775 through 0, 1 and 2. Copy 1 and 2 to the mode byte at $9166, but map 0 to mode 3; set the Space latch at $A776 so a held key does not repeat.
If $801E is nonzero, adjust the value loaded into sprite 5 Y at $8E07 by that amount; add when $801D is zero, subtract otherwise.
Up input raises $804C to a maximum of 2. Unless $0810 or $B113 blocks the rest, adjust the magnitude at $801E toward 3 or toward zero, changing $801D to zero when the opposite direction has stopped.
Down input lowers $804C to zero. Unless $0810 or $B114 blocks the rest, adjust the magnitude at $801E toward 3 or toward zero, changing $801D to $FF when the opposite direction has stopped.
On left input, if $B5B9 is $14 and $B5BA is zero, set $B5BB to $FF, $B5BA to 4 and $B5BC to zero; otherwise return without changing them.
On right input, if $B5B9 is $14 and $B5BA is zero, clear $B5BB, set $B5BA to 4 and clear $B5BC; otherwise return without changing them.

Use A to select a seven-byte record at $EB5C: one accumulator increment and three little-endian pointers. Clear the three $24-byte channel state blocks, initialize their pointers and counters from the selected record, clear SID registers, and enable the channel update flags.
Call the three-voice SID update at $E141, then call the separate routine at $E937 before returning.

If $E12E is nonzero, advance an eight-bit accumulator; on carry call $E3A3 for channel offsets $00, $24 and $48, then call $E43D for all three. For each enabled channel, write its stored frequency, pulse width, envelope and control values to the SID; finally write $E138 to $D418.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $E146. Initialization copies the selected record's first byte here; each enabled sound update adds it to the accumulator stored in the operand at $E14A.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E149 and the accumulator for the sound update. Initialization writes $FF here; the update stores each sum back. Carry from the addition controls whether it advances the three channel streams.

Twenty-four little-endian jump targets selected by the sound stream command dispatcher at $E42C. Some entries are zero; the nonzero entries point into the command handlers at $E256-$E3A2. The dispatcher writes the selected address into its jump operand.
Read a two-byte sequence-table base from the stream into indexed voice state, then select the first pointer in that table.

Add the indexed voice's offset to its sequence-table base and advance the offset. If the selected two-byte pointer is zero, reset to the first table entry; load the selected pointer into the stream pointer and continue reading.
Copy three bytes from the sound stream into indexed voice state at $E0DF-$E0E1, advance the stream pointer by three, set $E0E2 to one, and continue reading commands.
Select $80 for the indexed voice's $E0E3 state, then continue reading commands. The following entry points select $40, $20 or $10 instead.
Clear two indexed voice state bytes, take the next stream byte into $E0D9, advance the pointer and continue reading commands.

Set bit $20 in the indexed voice's $E0C2 state, clear $E0C9 and $E0CA, and copy three stream bytes to $E0CE-$E0D0. The $E341 entry sets bit $04 instead. Both advance the pointer by three and continue reading.
Copy two stream bytes to the indexed voice's $E0DC and $E0DB state, copy the second to $E0DD, advance the pointer by two, and set $E0DE to $40.
Clear the indexed voice's $E0DE state and continue reading the stream.
Set the low two bits of the indexed voice's $E0C2 state and continue reading the stream.

Count down the indexed voice's delay. When it expires, read its byte stream: values below $80 set the next value and reload the delay, $80-$BF dispatch through the command table, and higher values change stream parameters before reading again. Save the advanced pointer when a value is accepted.

For the channel selected by X, read a byte from the stream addressed by $E0CB/$E0CC plus $E0CD. A byte with bit 7 set resets the stream offset to $FF and has that bit cleared. Add $E0D3, the global offset at $E464 and $E0E5; use the result to select a little-endian frequency from $E5C2. The continuation at $E464 applies the channel's optional frequency and pulse adjustments and stores the resulting SID values in its state block.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E463. Initialization clears it; a sound-stream command at $E2C7 replaces it. The same routine then adds the channel byte at $E0E5, looks up a two-byte frequency and applies enabled pitch and pulse-width adjustments before storing the channel's frequency at $E0D6/$E0D7 and pulse width at $E0D8/$E0D9.

The first 82 little-endian values in the sound driver's frequency lookup. The driver doubles its index and reads a pair at $E46C and $E471; the sampled story, Broadway and outcome selections read within this portion. The table's full extent remains open.
The high byte of the first frequency value; the little-endian pairs begin one byte earlier at $E5C2 and continue through $E665.
Fourteen low bytes of pointers selected by a stream command at $E3EF; the corresponding high bytes start at $E676.
Fourteen high bytes paired with the low bytes at $E668, read by the command at $E3F5. The pointed-to data is not yet classified.
Update the shared modulation state, then call each active voice's effect routine according to the three flags at $E12F-$E131.

Update the first voice's timed effect. When its remaining count reaches zero, clear its active flag and envelope registers and set its completion flag. Otherwise count down the effect, periodically reload its frequency and add or subtract its configured frequency step before writing SID voice 1.
Update the second voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 2.
Update the third voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 3.
Clear the four sound flags at $E12E–$E131, then clear SID registers $D400–$D417. The following entry at $EB34 performs only the register clear.
Shift the four-byte state at $EB58-$EB5B, feeding in a value derived from $EB58 and the incoming carry; return the new byte at $EB58.

Three seven-byte records consumed by $E000, each holding one timing increment and three little-endian stream pointers. The airshaft success path selects record 1 and its failure paths select record 2; record 0's use remains open.

The stream and pointer bytes reached by selection 0 at $EB5C. In the opening-story snapshot, the active channel list pointers correspond to the three lists selected by this record. A 12,000-update simulation read this entire range; the stream-command format and the tune's full cycle remain open.
Stream and pointer bytes selected by record 1 at $EB63. The driver's three channels read these bytes while the airshaft success sound plays; the meaning of individual stream commands remains open.
Stream and pointer bytes selected by record 2 at $EB6A. The driver's three channels read these bytes while the airshaft failure sound plays; the meaning of individual stream commands remains open.
